```{r}
library(sf)
library(spatstat.geom)
library(sp)
load("BC_Animal.Rda")
sapply(DATA, class)
str(DATA$Animal)

```

```{r}
plot(DATA$Window, main = "Spatial Boundaries of BC")
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(spatstat))
plot(DATA$Elevation,main="Elevation Map of BC Animals")
coords <- DATA$Animal[,c("X","Y")]
window_sf <- st_as_sf(DATA$Window)
window <- as.owin(window_sf)
animal_ppp <- ppp(x = coords$X,
                y = coords$Y,
                window = window,
                )
# Run plot() on the resulting ppp object.
plot(animal_ppp)
```

```{r}
fig <- persp(DATA$Elevation,
      theta = 10,
      phi = 30,
      expand = 20,
      border = NA,
      shade = 0.7,
      lphi = 10,
      r = 10,
      box = FALSE,
      apron = TRUE,
      colmap  =terrain.colors(100),
      visible = TRUE,
      main = ""
)
x <- DATA$Animal$X
y <- DATA$Animal$Y
# Overlay the park locations.
perspPoints(x = x, y = y,
            Z = DATA$Elevation, M = fig,
            pch = 16, col = "blue", cex = 0.6)
plot(cut(DATA$Elevation,
         5),col = terrain.colors(5),
     main = "Elevation classes")

points(DATA$Animal$X, DATA$Animal$Y, pch = 16, col = "blue", cex = 0.6)

b <- quantile(DATA$Elevation, probs = (0:5)/5, type = 2, na.rm = TRUE)
Zcut <- cut(DATA$Elevation, breaks = b)


V <- tess(image = Zcut)


xrange <- range(c(DATA$Animal$X, DATA$Elevation$xrange))
yrange <- range(c(DATA$Animal$Y, DATA$Elevation$yrange))
custom_win <- owin(xrange = xrange, yrange = yrange)

animal_ppp_full <- ppp(x = DATA$Animal$X,
                       y = DATA$Animal$Y,
                       window = custom_win)

counts <- quadratcount(animal_ppp_full, tess = V)

table_counts <- as.table(counts)
table_counts

```

```{r}

# Calculate the median elevation within British Columbia and at animal locations
median_bc <- median(DATA$Elevation$v, na.rm = TRUE)
elev_at_animals <- interp.im(DATA$Elevation, DATA$Animal$X, DATA$Animal$Y)
median_animals <- median(elev_at_animals, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Median elevation in BC:", median_bc, "\n")
cat("Median elevation at animal locations:", median_animals, "\n")

# Generate KDE of elevation across BC
elev_all <- DATA$Elevation$v
elev_all <- elev_all[!is.na(elev_all)]

# Generate KDE of elevation at animal observation locations
elev_at_animals <- elev_at_animals[!is.na(elev_at_animals)]
kde_all <- density(elev_all)
kde_animals <- density(elev_at_animals)

# Plot both KDE distributions
plot(kde_all,
     main = "Elevation Distributions: BC vs. Animal Observations",
     xlab = "Elevation (meters)",
     ylab = "Density",
     col = "gray40", lwd = 2,
     xlim = range(c(kde_all$x, kde_animals$x)))
lines(kde_animals, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

# Add legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("BC (All Pixels)", "Animal Observations"),
       col = c("gray40", "blue"),
       lwd = 2)

# Identify both the highest and lowest elevation animal observations
elev_at_animals_full <- interp.im(DATA$Elevation, DATA$Animal$X, DATA$Animal$Y)
max_index <- which.max(elev_at_animals_full)
min_index <- which.min(elev_at_animals_full)

highest_animal <- DATA$Animal[max_index, ]
lowest_animal  <- DATA$Animal[min_index, ]

cat("Highest elevation animal observation:\n")
print(highest_animal)

cat("Lowest elevation animal observation:\n")
print(lowest_animal)


```

```{r}
# Compute the spatial intensity (points per km²) for animal observations
library(spatstat.explore)
# For example, a 10x10 grid
nx <- 10
ny <- 10
# Count points in each quadrat
Q <- quadratcount(animal_ppp, nx=nx, ny=ny)
intensity(Q)
quadrat.test(Q)
pp.animal.km <- rescale(animal_ppp, s = 1000, unitname = "km")
area_km <- area.owin(Window(pp.animal.km))
n_animals <- npoints(animal_ppp)
intensity <- n_animals / area_km
intensity
plot(animal_ppp , pch = 16, cols = "black", cex = 0.6)
# Overlay the quadrat grid
plot(Q, add = TRUE, col = "red")
```

```{r}
# Plot quadrat-based intensity and overlay animal locations
plot(intensity(Q, image = TRUE))
plot(animal_ppp, pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = "black", add = TRUE)

# Kernel density estimation using Diggle’s rule
kde <- density(animal_ppp, sigma = bw.ppl)

# Plot kernel density map with animal points
plot(kde, main = "Kernel Density of Animal Observation Intensity")
plot(animal_ppp, pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = "black", add = TRUE)

```

```{r}
# Perform kernel intensity estimation with cross-validated bandwidth and identify hotspots for animal observations
bw_cv <- bw.ppl(animal_ppp)
kde_cv <- scanLRTS(animal_ppp, r = bw_cv)
plot(kde_cv, main = "Intensity Estimate (bw.ppl cross-validation)")
hotspot_mask <- eval.im(pchisq(kde_cv, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE))
plot(Window(animal_ppp), add = TRUE, border = "darkgreen", lwd = 1)
plot(hotspot_mask)
plot(Window(animal_ppp), add = TRUE, border = "darkgreen", lwd = 1)

```

```{r}
# Estimate the relationship between animal intensity and elevation using rhohat
Zcut <- cut(DATA$Elevation, breaks = quantile(DATA$Elevation, probs = 0:4 / 4, type = 2))
animals <- unmark(animal_ppp)
quadratcount(animals, tess = tess(image = Zcut))
rho <- rhohat(animals, DATA$Elevation)
plot(rho)

```

```{r}
# Compute the inhomogeneous intensity surface for animal observations
lambda <- density(animal_ppp, sigma = bw.ppl, positive = TRUE)

# Generate Monte Carlo simulations for inhomogeneous K-function
en_K <- envelope(animal_ppp, Kinhom, simulate = expression(rpoispp(lambda)),
                 correction = "border", rank = 1, nsim = 19, fix.n = TRUE)

# Plot the K-function with simulation envelope
plot(en_K, main = "Ripley’s K-function with CSR Envelopes (Animal Observations)")


```

```{r}
# Compute intensity surface for animal observations
lambda <- density(animal_ppp, sigma = bw.ppl(animal_ppp), positive = TRUE)

# Generate simulation envelope for homogeneous pair correlation function
pcf_hom <- envelope(animal_ppp, pcf, simulate = expression(rpoispp(lambda)),
                    rank = 1, nsim = 19)

# Plot the homogeneous pair correlation function with envelope
plot(pcf_hom, main = "Pair Correlation Function (Homogeneous) - Animal Observations")
pcf_inhom <- envelope(animal_ppp, pcfinhom, nsim = 19,
                      simulate = expression(rpoispp(lambda)), rank = 1)

# Plot the inhomogeneous pair correlation function with simulation envelope
plot(pcf_inhom, main = "Inhomogeneous Pair Correlation Function (Animal Observations)")
```
